question: A person who spends 32% of his monthly income is able to save ₹7,752 per month. His monthly expenses (in ₹) are:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Savings** percentage = 100% − 32% = 68%

68% of **Income** = ₹7,752

**Monthly Expenses** (32%) = (7,752 ÷ 68) × 32

⇒ 114 × 32 = ₹3,648

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Spending** = 32% of **Monthly Income**

**Monthly Savings** = ₹7,752

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d17340c8277e053174c11cbb5c4783bd2ed064d994e1c1615c48629211871ec.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Income** = **Expenses** + **Savings**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Total Income** be ₹x.

⇒ **Savings** % = 100% − 32% = 68%

⇒ 68% of x = 7,752

⇒ (68 ÷ 100) × x = 7,752

⇒ x = (7,752 × 100) ÷ 68

⇒ x = 114 × 100 = ₹11,400 (**Monthly Income**)

⇒ **Monthly Expenses** = 32% of 11,400

⇒ **Monthly Expenses** = (32 ÷ 100) × 11,400

⇒ **Monthly Expenses** = 32 × 114 = ₹3,648

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change

When calculating values from a partial percentage, always identify the 100% base first. **Value** = (**Given Amount** ÷ **Given %**) × **Target %**.

Income-Expenditure Relation

**Savings** = **Income** − **Expenditure**. If expenditure increases by x% and income is constant, savings decrease by that absolute amount.

Ratio Method

Express percentages as fractions: 32% = 8/25. If **Income** is 25 units, **Expense** is 8 units and **Savings** is 17 units (25 − 8). 17 units = 7,752.
